question.text: The fund governance structure requires that the AIF be operated in the interest of:

answer.text: All investors, not only the sponsor, manager, or their directors/partners

explanation.text: The Logic: The Code of Conduct requires the AIF to be operated and managed in the interest of all investors, and not only in the interest of the sponsor, manager, directors or partners of the sponsor or manager, or any select investors. This is the core fiduciary/governance standard for an AIF. The Trap: Option A inverts the duty by aligning the fund with sponsor/manager interests. Option C narrows it to a single dominant investor, and Option D arbitrarily restricts the standard to Category I, both of which contradict the all-investors fiduciary rule. Note: Acts that favour the manager, sponsor or select investors over the broader investor base are governance breaches under the Code of Conduct.
